content: Purpose: To develop and assess a locally deployed multi-agent AI system for structuring radiology reports and ensuring quality assurance. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study analyzed 638 radiology reports from CT examinations of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, dictated by 15 board-certified radiologists in 2023 and 2024. A multi-agent AI pipeline was created to perform report structuring and quality assurance (QA). The system organized reports into standardized anatomical sections at the sentence level using regular expression rules and local large language models. It also identified mismatches between the Findings and Impression sections or within sections, gender-anatomy inconsistencies, and undocumented communication of critical findings. Two board-certified radiologists independently reviewed a subset of 45 reports. Results: The multi-agent system structured the Findings sections of all reports (22,270 sentences) into a predefined anatomical format while preserving the original content. The system flagged 90 reports (14.1%), most frequently for section mismatches (80 reports, 12.5%). In the radiologist evaluation, both reviewers agreed that 31 reports (69%) were correctly restructured, 2 reports (4%) were incorrectly restructured, and disagreed on 12 reports (27%). Both reviewers concurred that no clinically important information was omitted and no fabricated content was introduced. Overall QA performance was rated as "excellent" or "good" in 84% of evaluated reports, with the remainder rated as "fair." Conclusion: A locally deployed multi-agent AI system successfully integrated radiology report structuring and quality assurance into a single workflow. The system demonstrated favorable performance in radiologist evaluation and may support standardization and quality assurance in radiology practice.
